question: For Warrant 1 Condition A with at least two major-street lanes and one minor-street lane, what volumes must exist and over what time basis, and does meeting them compel signal installation?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For Warrant 1, Condition A (Minimum Vehicular Volume) with 2 or more major-street lanes and 1 minor-street lane, Table 4C-1 requires 600 vehicles per hour on the major street (total of both approaches) and 150 vehicles per hour on the more critical minor-street approach (one direction only) at the basic 100% level, existing for each of any 8 hours of an average day. The major-street and minor-street volumes must occur during the same 8 hours. Meeting these volumes does not compel signal installation — the warrant only means the need for a signal "should be considered" (Guidance) based on an engineering study; warrants are thresholds for study, not mandates to install. Standards (mandatory): - "These major-street and minor-street volumes shall be for the same 8 hours for each condition; however, the 8 hours that are selected for the Condition A analysis shall not be required to be the same 8 hours that are selected for the Condition B analysis." - "These major-street and minor-street volumes shall be for the same 8 hours for each condition; however, the 8 hours satisfied in Condition A shall not be required to be the same 8 hours satisfied in Condition B." - Table 4C-1 footnotes define the columns: "a Basic minimum hourly volume; b Used for combination of Conditions A and B after adequate trial of other remedial measures; c May be used when the major-street speed exceeds 40 mph or in an isolated community with a population of less than 10,000; d May be used for combination of Conditions A and B after adequate trial of other remedial measures when the major-street speed exceeds 40 mph or in an isolated community with a population of less than 10,000." Guidance (recommended): - Per the Guidance shown on the Section 4C.02 page, the need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that the 100 percent column volumes of Condition A (or Condition B) in Table 4C-1 exist on the major street and the more critical minor-street approach for each of any 8 hours of an average day — i.e., satisfying the warrant triggers consideration, not a requirement to install. Options (permitted): - The 70% columns (420 vph major / 105 vph minor for this lane combination) may be used in place of the 100% columns when the major-street speed exceeds 40 mph or in an isolated community with a population of less than 10,000. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 4C-1, Condition A, row "2 or more / 1": major-street volumes of 600 (100%), 480 (80%), 420 (70%), 336 (56%) vph and minor-street volumes of 150 (100%), 120 (80%), 105 (70%), 84 (56%) vph. - [Image 5] The full Section 4C.02 page shows the Guidance ("The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that one of the following conditions exist for each of any 8 hours of an average day") and the introductory text noting that warrants are not the only factor and installation decisions rest on an engineering study. Citations: - Section 4C.02 Standard §5 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Standard §10 (p.654) - Section 4C.02 Standard §56 (p.654) - Section 4C.02 Standard §42 (p.653) - Table 4C-1 (p.653) - Page 694
gold_answer: For each of the same 8 selected hours, 600 vph must exist on the major street (both approaches total) and 150 vph on the critical minor approach (one direction) at the 100-percent thresholds. Meeting the warrant does not compel installation; an engineering study must determine whether a signal is justified.
